tagline: Link design specs to code PRs and notify designers when code ships
metaTitle: GitHub + Figma Integration: Figma Specs on Pull Requests
metaDescription: Attach Figma specs to PRs, tell designers when their work ships, and track implementation status in Figma. GAIA links design and code. See the setup steps.
keywords: link Figma designs to GitHub PRs
intro:
Design and engineering teams work in parallel, with designers in Figma and developers in GitHub, but the handoff between the two is rarely smooth. Developers hunt for the right frame while the designer has already moved to the next screen. Designers have no idea when their designs have shipped to production. Reviews happen in separate tools with no shared context, and version mismatches between the design file and the live implementation go unnoticed until QA catches them.

GAIA links the two to create a continuous connection between design specifications and the code that implements them. When a developer opens a pull request, GAIA can automatically attach the relevant frame or component as a comment on the pull request, so reviewers can compare design intent against implementation without leaving GitHub. When that pull request merges, GAIA notifies the designer in Figma (or via their preferred channel) so they can verify the implementation and sign off.

This is well suited to product teams practicing design-led development. Designers stay in the loop on engineering progress without polling developers, developers always have the right spec attached to their pull request, and nothing ships that the design team hasn't been able to review.

useCases.title: Attach design specs to pull requests automatically
useCases.description: When a developer opens a pull request, GAIA searches for the matching frame based on the branch name, pull request title, or a link to the frame in the pull request body, then posts a direct preview link as a comment so reviewers can compare implementation against design intent without switching tools.

useCases.title: Notify designers when their designs ship
useCases.description: GAIA watches for merged pull requests that implement specific components or screens, and sends a notification to the responsible designer via comments in the design file, Slack, or email so they can verify the live implementation matches the approved design.

useCases.title: Track design implementation status in Figma
useCases.description: GAIA updates frame annotations or comments with pull request status (open, in review, merged, or reverted), giving designers a real-time implementation tracker directly inside their design files.

useCases.title: Flag design-code mismatches for review
useCases.description: When a component is updated after a related pull request has already been merged, GAIA creates an issue flagging the potential discrepancy between the new design and the shipped code so the team can decide whether to update the implementation.

useCases.title: Generate design change changelogs for repositories
useCases.description: When a designer publishes a new version of a component library, GAIA posts a summary of the changes as an issue or pull request comment on affected repositories so developers know which components may need implementation updates.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Figma to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Link your repositories and team design files through GAIA's integration settings. GAIA uses GitHub OAuth and a Figma personal access token to read file structures and post comments without needing editor permissions.

Tell GAIA how to match branches or pull requests to design pages and frames, whether by naming convention, explicit links in pull request descriptions, or component names. You can configure notification preferences for designers per file or page.

howItWorks.step: GAIA bridges design and code automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA handles communication between the two tools continuously. Design specs appear on pull requests without developer effort, and designers receive automatic updates when their work ships, with no Slack pings or status meetings required.

faqs.question: Does GAIA need editor access to our Figma files?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA only requires viewer access to read file structure, frame names, and component information, and commenter access to post status updates. It never modifies your design files without explicit permission.

faqs.question: How does GAIA match a pull request to the right frame?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses several matching strategies: a link to the frame pasted in the pull request description, branch names that follow a convention like 'feature/component-name', pull request labels, or a direct mapping table you configure in GAIA. The most reliable method is including a link to the frame in your pull request template.

faqs.question: Can GAIA work with component libraries across multiple files?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can track components across multiple design files and link them to the appropriate repositories. This is particularly useful for design systems where a shared component library is consumed by multiple product repos.
